title: Endpoint bound for the Gaussian profile
statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $C>0$ such that for all $p\in[0,1]$, all real $b$ equal to $0$ or $1$, the closed Gaussian profile satisfies $U(p)\le \varepsilon+C|p-b|$.
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $C>0$ such that $\overline I(p)\le\varepsilon+C|p-b|$ for all $p\in[0,1]$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$.
